parts.title: The Brassica Family: One Plant, Many Vegetables
parts.article:
The Brassica Family One Plant, Many Vegetables

(A) Many people are surprised to learn that cabbage, broccoli, cauliflower, kale, Brussels sprouts and kohlrabi all belong to the same plant family. Although these vegetables differ greatly in appearance, taste and texture, they all originated from a single wild plant called Brassica oleracea. This species, commonly known as wild cabbage or wild mustard, has grown naturally along the rocky coastlines of Europe for thousands of years. Through careful human selection, it has gradually developed into many of the vegetables that are commonly found in supermarkets today.

(B) The transformation of Brassica oleracea did not happen by chance. It was the result of a process known as selective breeding, in which farmers repeatedly chose plants with desirable characteristics and used them to produce the next generation. Unlike modern genetic engineering, selective breeding does not involve changing a plant’s DNA in a laboratory. Instead, it relies on naturally occurring genetic variation that already exists within a species.

(C) Early farmers noticed that some wild Brassica plants had larger leaves, thicker stems or more compact flower buds than others. By saving seeds only from those preferred plants, they gradually increased the frequency of these characteristics over many generations. As a result, different vegetables began to emerge. Cabbage was developed for its large terminal leaves, broccoli for its flower buds, cauliflower for its undeveloped flower clusters, Brussels sprouts for its side buds, kale for its loose leaves and kohlrabi for its swollen stem.

(D) Although these vegetables look very different, scientists have discovered that they are genetically very similar. Because they all belong to the same species, they are still capable of interbreeding under suitable conditions. This close genetic relationship explains why plant breeders can continue to develop new varieties with improved qualities, such as better taste, higher nutritional value or greater resistance to disease.

(E) The Brassica family is also well known for its impressive nutritional benefits. Most Brassica vegetables contain large amounts of vitamins C and K, dietary fibre and important minerals such as potassium and calcium. They also contain natural plant chemicals called glucosinolates, which give these vegetables their distinctive flavour. When a Brassica vegetable is cut or chewed, these compounds are converted into other substances that may help protect the body from certain diseases. Although researchers continue to investigate these effects, many health experts recommend eating a variety of Brassica vegetables as part of a balanced diet.

(F) However, growing Brassica crops presents several challenges for farmers. Because many members of the family are closely related, they are vulnerable to similar insects and plant diseases. One of the most serious problems is clubroot disease, which attacks the roots and reduces plant growth. Farmers often reduce these risks by rotating crops, improving soil conditions and developing resistant varieties through breeding programmes.

(G) Modern plant scientists now combine traditional breeding methods with advanced genetic techniques. By studying the DNA of Brassica plants, researchers can identify genes responsible for useful characteristics such as drought tolerance, faster growth or resistance to pests. This knowledge enables breeders to produce improved crops more efficiently while still relying on natural breeding methods. Scientists are also preserving wild Brassica populations because they contain valuable genetic diversity that may help future crops adapt to climate change and new diseases.

(H) The history of the Brassica family demonstrates the remarkable influence of human agriculture on plant evolution. From one wild coastal plant, centuries of careful selection have produced a wide range of vegetables with different shapes, colours and uses. Today, Brassica crops are grown throughout the world and play an important role in both human nutrition and global agriculture. Their development provides a clear example of how small genetic differences, guided by human choice, can create extraordinary diversity while maintaining a common biological origin.

questions.question: All Brassica vegetables originated from more than one wild plant.

analyses.content: 原文明确说明这些蔬菜都起源于“单一的野生植物”（a single wild plant），而题目说“多于一种”（more than one），两者完全相反。
你可能没注意到原文里的“a single”，凭借常识误以为这么多不同种类的蔬菜肯定来自多个不同的植物。

(A) Many people are surprised to learn that cabbage, broccoli, cauliflower, kale, Brussels sprouts and kohlrabi all belong to the same plant family. Although these vegetables differ greatly in appearance, taste and texture, they all originated from a single wild plant called Brassica oleracea.

questions.question: Selective breeding changes a plant’s DNA directly in a laboratory.

analyses.content: 原文直接否定了这一点，指出选择性繁育“不涉及”（does not involve）在实验室里改变植物DNA。
你可能把“现代基因工程”（modern genetic engineering）的做法张冠李戴，误当成了题干里问的“选择性繁育”（selective breeding）。

It was the result of a process known as selective breeding, in which farmers repeatedly chose plants with desirable characteristics and used them to produce the next generation. Unlike modern genetic engineering, selective breeding does not involve changing a plant’s DNA in a laboratory. Instead, it relies on naturally occurring genetic variation that already exists within a species.

questions.question: Early farmers repeatedly selected plants with desirable characteristics.

analyses.content: 原文明确提到农民“反复挑选具有理想特征的植物”（repeatedly chose plants with desirable characteristics），与题目表述完全一致。
你可能在找“Early farmers”时定位到了下一段，但其实这里（句5）已经把核心动作和目的讲得一清二楚了。

(B) The transformation of Brassica oleracea did not happen by chance. It was the result of a process known as selective breeding, in which farmers repeatedly chose plants with desirable characteristics and used them to produce the next generation.

questions.question: Broccoli and cauliflower were developed from different wild species.

analyses.content: 原文第一段就强调了包括西兰花（broccoli）和花椰菜（cauliflower）在内的这些蔬菜，全部起源于“同一个野生物种”（a single wild plant）。
你可能被后面段落里它们各自不同的外观特征描述迷惑了，误以为差异大的蔬菜就一定来自不同的野生物种。

(A) Many people are surprised to learn that cabbage, broccoli, cauliflower, kale, Brussels sprouts and kohlrabi all belong to the same plant family. Although these vegetables differ greatly in appearance, taste and texture, they all originated from a single wild plant called Brassica oleracea.

questions.question: Brassica vegetables are generally considered nutritious.

analyses.content: 原文明确指出这个家族的植物以“令人印象深刻的营养价值”（impressive nutritional benefits）而闻名。
你可能在纠结原文没有直接出现“generally considered”（普遍认为）这个词，但“well known for”（因...而众所周知）完全可以表达出大家公认有营养的意思。

(E) The Brassica family is also well known for its impressive nutritional benefits. Most Brassica vegetables contain large amounts of vitamins C and K, dietary fibre and important minerals such as potassium and calcium.

questions.question: Clubroot disease mainly damages the roots of Brassica plants.

analyses.content: 原文清楚写明根肿病会“攻击根部”（attacks the roots），这与题目说主要破坏植物根部完美契合。
你可能会因为原文还附加了“减少植物生长”（reduces plant growth）而犹豫，但“攻击根部”这个核心事实是正确且被明确提到的。

Because many members of the family are closely related, they are vulnerable to similar insects and plant diseases. One of the most serious problems is clubroot disease, which attacks the roots and reduces plant growth. Farmers often reduce these risks by rotating crops, improving soil conditions and developing resistant varieties through breeding programmes.

questions.question: Scientists have completely replaced traditional breeding with genetic engineering.

analyses.content: 原文说科学家是将传统方法与先进技术“结合”（combine），并且仍然依赖（still relying on）自然繁育方法，而不是“完全替代”（completely replaced）。
你可能看到科学家使用了“先进基因技术”就脑补了传统方法被淘汰，忽略了原文里的“combine”一词。

(G) Modern plant scientists now combine traditional breeding methods with advanced genetic techniques. By studying the DNA of Brassica plants, researchers can identify genes responsible for useful characteristics such as drought tolerance, faster growth or resistance to pests. This knowledge enables breeders to produce improved crops more efficiently while still relying on natural breeding methods.

analyses.content: 题目问农民挑选植物是因为它们展现了什么，原文明确说到挑选的是具有“理想特征”（desirable characteristics）的植物。
你可能会去找“saved seeds”所在的后续句子，但填空词的具体修饰语“desirable”直接将答案锁死在了第5句。

(B) The transformation of Brassica oleracea did not happen by chance. It was the result of a process known as selective breeding, in which farmers repeatedly chose plants with desirable characteristics and used them to produce the next generation.
原文在列举各蔬菜特征时，明确说到苤蓝（kohlrabi）是因其“膨大的茎”（swollen stem）而被专门培育出来的。
你可能在看这一长串并列排比句时看花了眼，其实只要准确定位“kohlrabi”和“swollen”，紧跟在后面的词就是答案。

As a result, different vegetables began to emerge. Cabbage was developed for its large terminal leaves, broccoli for its flower buds, cauliflower for its undeveloped flower clusters, Brussels sprouts for its side buds, kale for its loose leaves and kohlrabi for its swollen stem.
原文直接列举了这类蔬菜含有的成分，包括维生素、矿物质以及“膳食纤维”（dietary fibre）。
你可能看到了potassium和calcium，但题目空格前有“dietary”作为限定词，所以必须填fibre才能匹配。

(E) The Brassica family is also well known for its impressive nutritional benefits. Most Brassica vegetables contain large amounts of vitamins C and K, dietary fibre and important minerals such as potassium and calcium.
原文直接说明了一种叫做glucosinolates的天然植物化学物质赋予了这些蔬菜独特的风味（distinctive flavour）。
这个词虽然很长很生僻，但你千万不要因为不认识就不敢填，填空题非常喜欢考这种由“known as / called”引出的专有名词。

Most Brassica vegetables contain large amounts of vitamins C and K, dietary fibre and important minerals such as potassium and calcium. They also contain natural plant chemicals called glucosinolates, which give these vegetables their distinctive flavour. When a Brassica vegetable is cut or chewed, these compounds are converted into other substances that may help protect the body from certain diseases.
题目问农民通过什么方式控制疾病，原文明确指出农民通过“轮作”（rotating crops）来降低风险。
你可能想填“improving”或“developing”，但空格后面紧跟着的是“crops”，因此必须选择与之固定搭配的rotating。

One of the most serious problems is clubroot disease, which attacks the roots and reduces plant growth. Farmers often reduce these risks by rotating crops, improving soil conditions and developing resistant varieties through breeding programmes.
题目问保留野生植物是因为它们包含什么宝贵的遗传物质，原文直接给出答案是“遗传多样性”（genetic diversity）。
你可能会被后面的“climate change”或“diseases”吸引走注意力，但题目空格前有“valuable genetic”限定，直接锁定了diversity。

This knowledge enables breeders to produce improved crops more efficiently while still relying on natural breeding methods. Scientists are also preserving wild Brassica populations because they contain valuable genetic diversity that may help future crops adapt to climate change and new diseases.
